compute category response probabilities and derivatives under the partial credit model

Source: R/fct_cat_engine_pcm.R
compute_pi_pcm.Rd

returns the category response probabilities for a given ability value and a
given matrix of item parameters under Masters partial credit model (PCM)
returns the first derivatives of the category response probabilities

Usage

compute_pi_pcm(theta, bank, D = 1)

Arguments

theta

ability

bank

item parameters one row per item
columns 1 to m hold the step parameters delta_j1 to delta_jm
there is no discrimination column because the partial credit model is a
Rasch model
the steps are free for every item which is what separates this model from
the rating scale model where the steps of item j are lambda_j+delta_k so
all the items have the same spacing of steps and differ only by lambda_j
delta_jk is the value of theta where the curves of the categories k-1 and
k cross
the steps do not need to be ordered
when delta_j2 is below delta_j1 category 1 is never the most probable
category but every probability stays positive which is not the case for
the graded response model
an item with fewer categories than the widest item is padded with NA
a mirt model fitted with itemtype="Rasch" gives the bank with the b1 to bm
columns of mirt::coef(model,IRTpars=TRUE,simplify=TRUE)$items to be used with D=1
mirt stores a dichotomous item in column b instead of b1 so it has to be
moved to the first column

D

metric constant can be 1 or 1.702

Value

Pi category response probabilities one row per item one column per category
dPi first derivatives of the category response probabilities exact when D=1
and divided by D as in catR otherwise

Note

this function should return the same result as catR::Pi(model="PCM")
the number of response categories is ncol(bank)+1 so a 5 point Likert scale
scored 0 1 2 3 4 needs a bank with 4 columns
the probability of category k is
P(X=k|theta)=exp(sum_t=1^k D*(theta-delta_jt))/sum over all categories
with the empty sum for category 0 equal to zero
the rating scale model is the partial credit model with
delta_jk=lambda_j+delta_k
adding an item discrimination to the partial credit model gives the
generalized partial credit model
in the code gamma holds exp(sum_t=1^k D*(theta-delta_jt)) for each category and
v holds the category score k
the exponent of category k grows by D*k when theta grows by one so the exact
derivative of gamma is gamma*D*v
catR uses gamma*v and so does this function to return the same result
with D=1 the two are identical and with D=1.702 dPi is too small by a factor
of D and the information by a factor of D^2 which leaves the item selection
and the EAP estimates unchanged

Examples

bank<-matrix(c(-1.853,-2.214,-0.936,-1.508,-0.412,
               -0.627,-0.504,-1.215,-0.183,0.338,
               0.418,0.692,0.284,0.735,1.102,
               1.636,1.927,1.405,2.118,2.285),
             nrow=5,
             dimnames=list(c(1,2,3,4,5),
                           c("deltaj1","deltaj2","deltaj3","deltaj4")))
pi_cat<-catR::Pi(th=0,bank,model="PCM")
pi<-compute_pi_pcm(theta=0,bank)
pi_cat
